sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Meg Bernhardt and I'm a contributor to The New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫梅格·伯恩哈特，我是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: This is a story about grief, which I write a lot about.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于悲伤的故事，我经常写这个主题。

sentences.en: But it's about a particular kind of grief.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个关于特定种类悲伤的故事。

sentences.en: Grief of the world moving on from a mass trauma event when you don't feel capable of doing so yourself.
sentences.zh: 当周围人已经从群体创伤事件中走出来，而你觉得自己无法做到时，那种被世界抛下的悲伤。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of reporting on how this moment in the pandemic is affecting people with disabilities, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，有很多报道关注大流行的这一时期如何影响残障人士。

sentences.en: And I was curious about what the experience of moving on from COVID looks like for low-income families.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，低收入家庭走出新冠阴影的经历是怎样的。

sentences.en: And in this case, a community composed predominantly of Black and Latino families.
sentences.zh: 在这个案例中，是一个主要由黑人和拉丁裔家庭组成的社区。

sentences.en: Through previous reporting, I became familiar with the school in South Central Los Angeles called 95th Street Elementary School.
sentences.zh: 通过之前的报道，我熟悉了洛杉矶中南部一所名为95街小学的学校。

sentences.en: Like in other poor communities in LA, families here have suffered disproportionately during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 就像洛杉矶的其他贫困社区一样，这里的家庭在大流行期间遭受了不成比例的苦难。

sentences.en: Vaccination rates are low, in part due to government mistruSt.
sentences.zh: 疫苗接种率很低，部分原因是对政府缺乏信任。

sentences.en: 94% of students live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 94%的学生生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: And so, for the Sunday read you're about to hear, I followed this school community for more than half a year.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于你们接下来将听到的“周日特读”，我跟随这个学校社区度过了半年多的时间。

sentences.en: As students, teachers, and parents grappled with the pressure to return to normal.
sentences.zh: 当时学生、老师和家长都在努力应对回归常态的压力。

sentences.en: While still dealing with the physical and emotional fallout of COVID.
sentences.zh: 同时还要应对新冠带来的身体和情感余波。

sentences.en: I first visited 95th Street Elementary on a sunny day last October.
sentences.zh: 我第一次访问95街小学是在去年10月的一个晴朗日子里。

sentences.en: It was Día de los Muertos.
sentences.zh: 那是亡灵节。

sentences.en: And the first floor hallway was filled with papier-mâché crafts and altars that students had made honoring their dead loved ones.
sentences.zh: 一楼的走廊里摆满了纸扎工艺品和学生们为纪念逝去亲人而制作的祭坛。

sentences.en: There was a trick-or-treat event where teachers set up their cars on the blacktop and opened up their trunks.
sentences.zh: 有一个不给糖就捣蛋的活动，老师们把车停在沥青操场上，打开后备箱。

sentences.en: And kids would walk around in their costumes, collecting candy.
sentences.zh: 孩子们穿着化装服走来走去，收集糖果。

sentences.en: As I hung around talking with staff members and parents, I could see that there was just a huge sense of loss in the community.
sentences.zh: 当我四处闲逛、与教职员工和家长交谈时，我能看出社区里弥漫着巨大的失落感。

sentences.en: One woman told me she lost her sister during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 一位妇女告诉我，她在疫情期间失去了妹妹。

sentences.en: Another lost her brother to suicide, which she attributes, in part, to the economic stresses of COVID.
sentences.zh: 另一个人失去了弟弟，他死于自杀，她将这部分归咎于新冠带来的经济压力。

sentences.en: Others told me about grandparents dying.
sentences.zh: 其他人向我讲述了祖父母的去世。

sentences.en: About losing their parents.
sentences.zh: 关于失去父母。

sentences.en: There were teachers with underlying health conditions that made them terrified of the physical realities of this virus.
sentences.zh: 有些老师有基础健康状况，这让他们对这种病毒的现实物理威胁感到恐惧。

sentences.en: The pandemic, one person told me, just felt like funeral after funeral after funeral.
sentences.zh: 一个人告诉我，大流行感觉就像一场接一场又一场的葬礼。

sentences.en: I thought about the family social scientist, Pauline Boss.
sentences.zh: 我想到了家庭社会学家保琳·博斯。

sentences.en: Back in 2021, I wrote a profile of Boss, who coined the term, ambiguous loss.
sentences.zh: 早在2021年，我就写过一篇关于博斯的个人简介，她创造了“模棱两可的损失”这个词。

sentences.en: It refers to losses in which someone is physically present, but psychologically absent.
sentences.zh: 它是指一个人在身体上存在但在心理上缺席的损失。

sentences.en: Or the reverse.
sentences.zh: 或者反过来。

sentences.en: Situations of loss that are sort of unclear and defy our ideas of closure, like missing in action fighter pilots or dementia.
sentences.zh: 这种损失情况有些模糊，违背了我们对释怀的认知，比如失踪的战斗机飞行员或痴呆症。

sentences.en: With ambiguous loss comes what Boss calls the myth of closure.
sentences.zh: 伴随着模棱两可的损失而来的，是博斯所说的“释怀的神话”。

sentences.en: This idea that we can follow certain steps of grieving and then we'll go forward into our productive lives.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，我们可以遵循某些悲伤的步骤，然后就能昂首迈入富有成效的生活。

sentences.en: And at this point in the pandemic, we're hearing in culture and policy that we've made it through COVID.
sentences.zh: 而在大流行的这个阶段，我们在文化和政策中听到的是，我们已经熬过了新冠。

sentences.en: So let's go back to how we were in 2019.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们回到2019年的状态吧。

sentences.en: But for the community at 95th Street Elementary School, they experienced so much grief and death and illness and trauma.
sentences.zh: 但对于95街小学的社区来说，他们经历了如此多的悲伤、死亡、疾病和创伤。

sentences.en: It's difficult for the people I talked to at the school to map their reality onto this push for a return to normal.
sentences.zh: 我在学校里交谈过的人很难将他们的现实与这种重回常态的推动力对应起来。

sentences.en: And they're trying to find a way to make their own narrative.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图找到一种方法来书写自己的故事。

sentences.en: So, here's my article.
sentences.zh: 那么，这就是我的文章。

sentences.en: The school where the pandemic never ended.
sentences.zh: 那所大流行从未结束的学校。

sentences.en: Read by Samantha Dez.
sentences.zh: 由萨曼莎·德兹朗读。

sentences.en: At 7.30 on a crisp January morning, Lakeisha Fell Davis was at the wheel of her car, driving to Westmont, a community in the southern part of Los Angeles County.
sentences.zh: 在一个清爽的1月早晨7点半，拉基莎·费尔·戴维斯开着车，前往洛杉矶县南部的一个社区威斯特蒙特。

sentences.en: She was headed to 95th Street Elementary School, where she is both a substitute teacher and a parent of two students.
sentences.zh: 她正前往95街小学，她在那里既是一名代课老师，也是两个学生的家长。

sentences.en: Her daughter, Michaela, who was then nine, nibbled on a bagel.
sentences.zh: 她的女儿米凯拉当时九岁，正在啃一个贝果。

sentences.en: Kevin Jr., her seven-year-old son, looked out the window at the succession of strip malls, body shops, and liquor stores.
sentences.zh: 她的七岁儿子小凯文看着窗外接连不断的购物中心、汽车修理厂和烟酒店。

sentences.en: Surgical masks were tucked next to their seats, and disinfectant wipes sat in the central console.
sentences.zh: 医用口罩塞在他们的座位旁，消毒湿巾放在中央扶手上。

sentences.en: Glancing at her children in the rearview mirror, Fell Davis began a prayer for her children's safety.
sentences.zh: 费尔·戴维斯从后视镜里瞥了一眼孩子们，开始为孩子们的安全祈祷。

sentences.en: But she couldn't help picturing the classrooms, the cafeteria, the schoolyard.
sentences.zh: 但她情不自禁地脑补出那些教室、食堂和学校操场。

sentences.en: All those kids, all those teachers, any one of them potentially carrying COVID-19, and breathing the same air as she and her children.
sentences.zh: 所有那些孩子，所有那些老师，他们中的任何一个人都可能携带新冠病毒，并与她和她的孩子呼吸着同样的空气。

sentences.en: Fell Davis was aware that at this point in 2023, most people treated the pandemic as a thing of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 费尔·戴维斯意识到，到了2023年的这个节点，大多数人都把大流行当作过去的事情来对待。

sentences.en: For her, though, COVID still poses a real threat.
sentences.zh: 然而对她来说，新冠仍然构成了真正的威胁。

sentences.en: Fell Davis has type 1 diabetes, putting her at higher risk of hospitalization and long-term complications from illness.
sentences.zh: 费尔·戴维斯患有1型糖尿病，这使她因生病而住院和产生长期并发症的风险更高。

sentences.en: As such, her experience during the pandemic has shaped how she thinks about her daily life,
sentences.zh: 因此，她在疫情期间的经历塑造了她对日常生活的看法，

sentences.en: especially at 95th Street, where she has worked on and off for more than a decade as a substitute teacher and teaching assistant.
sentences.zh: 特别是在95街学校，她作为代课老师和助教断断续续在那里工作了十多年。

sentences.en: A COVID diagnosis has potentially disastrous physical, emotional, and financial ramifications for her family.
sentences.zh: 确诊新冠对她的家庭来说可能带来灾难性的身体、情感和财务后果。

sentences.en: She felt much more comfortable when schools in the Los Angeles Unified District were online during the first year and a half of the pandemic, and her kids were attending virtually.
sentences.zh: 当洛杉矶联合学区在疫情头一年半实行网课、她的孩子通过虚拟方式上学时，她觉得自在多了。

sentences.en: Sure, they missed their friends, but Michaela and Kevin were both shy and soft-spoken children who had never really strayed far from home.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们想念朋友，但米凯拉和小凯文都是害羞且轻声细语的孩子，从未真正远离过家。

sentences.en: They didn't seem to mind the arrangement.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎并不介意这种安排。

sentences.en: And back then, Fell Davis' mother, who was paralyzed on her left side after surviving stomach cancer and two strokes,
sentences.zh: 而在当时，费尔·戴维斯的母亲在战胜胃癌和两次中风后左侧瘫痪，

sentences.en: could visit them with relative peace of mind despite her poor health.
sentences.zh: 尽管健康状况不佳，她还是能够相对安心地去探望他们。

sentences.en: Her fears were confirmed in the winter of 2021, when her husband, Kevin, caught COVID.
sentences.zh: 2021年冬天，她的丈夫凯文感染了新冠，她的恐惧得到了证实。

sentences.en: He was out of his security guard job for over a week, with only partial sick pay, plunging them into a brief period of financial stress.
sentences.zh: 他因为保安工作停工了一周多，只有部分病假工资，这让他们陷入了短暂的经济压力期。

sentences.en: Credit card bills were due, as was her husband's life insurance payment.
sentences.zh: 信用卡账单到期了，她丈夫的人寿保险费也是如此。

sentences.en: The entire family got sick.
sentences.zh: 全家人都生病了。

sentences.en: Am I going to die?
sentences.zh: 我会死吗？

sentences.en: Kevin Jr.
sentences.zh: 小凯文

sentences.en: asked.
sentences.zh: 问。

sentences.en: The pandemic had overshadowed most of his young life and took its toll on his psyche.
sentences.zh: 大流行笼罩了他童年的大部分时间，并对他的精神造成了沉重打击。

sentences.en: He would become agitated, sometimes crying, if he saw someone who wasn't wearing a mask.
sentences.zh: 如果他看到有人没戴口罩，他就会变得焦躁不安，有时甚至会哭泣。

sentences.en: Even as Fell Davis assured him that he wouldn't die, her bout with the virus confined her to her bedroom for three days with body aches and a fever.
sentences.zh: 尽管费尔·戴维斯向他保证他不会死，但她自己的一场病毒感染让她全身酸痛并发烧，被困在卧室里三天。

sentences.en: Horrified that his mother couldn't get out of bed, the boy asked instead if she was going to die.
sentences.zh: 由于惊恐于母亲无法下床，这个男孩转而问她是不是快要死了。

sentences.en: Fell Davis cried when she learned that in the fall of 2021,
sentences.zh: 当得知2021年秋天，

sentences.en: LAUSD would require students and teachers to return to in-person learning.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶联合学区将要求学生和老师返校进行线下上课时，费尔·戴维斯哭了。

sentences.en: Her home, a cozy two-bedroom apartment in a calm neighborhood, had become her haven, the place where she had more control over her family's health than she had anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 她的家，一个位于安静社区里的舒适两居室公寓，已经成了她的避难所，在这里她比在其他任何地方都更能掌控自己家庭的健康。

sentences.en: She was stressed about whether she might get sick, but she was also nervous about the vaccines, which the district had mandated for most employees.
sentences.zh: 她对是否会生病感到压力山大，但她也对学区强制大多数员工接种的疫苗感到紧张。

sentences.en: What was in them, she wondered, and how were they made so quickly?
sentences.zh: 她想，里面有什么成分，它们是怎么这么快被制造出来的？

sentences.en: But she decided that she had to go back.
sentences.zh: 但她决定自己必须回去。

sentences.en: Her husband couldn't handle the bills himself, and while she preferred that her children learn remotely for as long as the pandemic lasted,
sentences.zh: 她丈夫无法独自应对账单，虽然她更希望孩子们只要疫情还在持续就远程上学，

sentences.en: she also wanted them to know how to carry themselves among other people.
sentences.zh: 但她也希望他们知道如何在其他人中间表现自己。

sentences.en: To her son, anything outside the apartment was scary.
sentences.zh: 对她的儿子来说，公寓外面的任何东西都是可怕的。

sentences.en: If he didn't have a mask on in public, he'd put his shirt over his mouth, as if hiding.
sentences.zh: 如果他在公共场合没戴口罩，他就会把衬衫拉到嘴上，仿佛在躲藏一样。

sentences.en: She didn't want to raise him to fear the world.
sentences.zh: 她不想把他培养成一个害怕世界的人。

sentences.en: As Fell Davis turned down 96th Street, parents and grandparents and aunts and uncles walked kids to the school fence.
sentences.zh: 当费尔·戴维斯拐入96街时，爸爸妈妈、爷爷奶奶和叔叔阿姨们正陪着孩子们走向学校的栅栏。

sentences.en: The families at 95th Street Elementary were mostly Black and Latino.
sentences.zh: 95街小学的家庭大多是黑人和拉丁裔。

sentences.en: Except, teachers like to point out, for the Russian family that enrolled a few years back.
sentences.zh: 正如老师们喜欢指出的那样，几年前入学的那个俄罗斯家庭除外。

sentences.en: Looking once more at her children through the rearview mirror,
sentences.zh: 透过后视镜再次看着她的孩子们，

sentences.en: Fell Davis reminded them of her rules.
sentences.zh: 费尔·戴维斯提醒他们注意她的规矩。

sentences.en: Wash your hands, wear your masks, don't share snacks.
sentences.zh: 洗手，戴口罩，不要分享零食。

sentences.en: At 95th Street, 94% of students live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 在95街，94%的学生生活在贫困中。

sentences.en: Many parents work essential jobs and suffer from chronic illness.
sentences.zh: 许多父母从事基础工作，并患有慢性疾病。

sentences.en: The school and other poor communities in Los Angeles have suffered disproportionately during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这所学校和洛杉矶的其他贫困社区在大流行期间遭受了不成比例的苦难。

sentences.en: In California, where the earnings gap between high and low-income families is among the widest in the country, the pandemic has clarified inequality's consequences.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州，高收入家庭和低收入家庭之间的收入差距全国最大，大流行已经阐明了不平等的后果。

sentences.en: The life expectancy for Latinos in California has decreased by approximately six years.
sentences.zh: 加州拉丁裔的预期寿命缩短了大约六年。

sentences.en: For Black Californians, four years.
sentences.zh: 对于加州的黑人来说，是四年。

sentences.en: In Los Angeles County, where Latinos make up nearly half the population, their overall mortality rate has increased more than any other racial or ethnic group.
sentences.zh: 在拉丁裔占人口近一半的洛杉矶县，他们的总体死亡率增长幅度超过了任何其他种族或族裔群体。

sentences.en: Among the hardest-hit areas have been East and South Los Angeles, which are home to lower-income Latino and Black families who work essential jobs,
sentences.zh: 受打击最严重的地区之一是洛杉矶东部和南部，这里是低收入拉丁裔和黑人家庭的家园，他们从事基础工作，

sentences.en: may live in multi-generational houses without room to distance, and suffer higher rates of chronic illnesses, like asthma and diabetes.
sentences.zh: 可能住在没有空间保持社交距离的多代同堂房屋中，并且患有哮喘和糖尿病等慢性疾病的比例更高。

sentences.en: In Westmont, 384 of every 100,000 residents have died of COVID, compared with 113 in the affluent west side neighborhood of Brentwood, near UCLA.
sentences.zh: 在威斯特蒙特，每10万名居民中有384人死于新冠，相比之下，靠近加州大学洛杉矶分校的布伦特wood富裕西区社区这一数字为113人。

sentences.en: But elsewhere in Los Angeles, and the rest of the country, most people have embraced the return to normal so central to the nation's idea of COVID recovery.
sentences.zh: 但在洛杉矶的其他地方以及全国其他地区，大多数人已经接受了对国家新冠恢复理念至关重要的“回归常态”。

sentences.en: Before the start of the new school year,
sentences.zh: 在新学年开始之前，

sentences.en: LAUSD rolled back most of its remaining COVID protocols, doing away with mandatory masking and testing.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶联合学区撤销了大部分剩余的新冠防疫规程，取消了强制戴口罩和检测的规定。

sentences.en: In an interview that aired in September,
sentences.zh: 在9月份播出的一个采访中，

sentences.en: President Biden declared the pandemic over.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统宣布大流行已经结束。

sentences.en: At the end of February, California's governor, Gavin Newsom, retired the state's pandemic emergency declaration.
sentences.zh: 2月底，加州州长加文·纽森废除了该州的疫情紧急状态。

sentences.en: And in May, the federal government is anticipated to do the same for the country at large.
sentences.zh: 并且在5月份，预计联邦政府也会对全国采取同样的举措。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, after protracted debate and delays, conversation about California's adding COVID-19 to its list of mandatory vaccines for schoolchildren died down.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，经过长时间的辩论和拖延，关于加州将新冠肺炎加入学童强制疫苗名单的讨论逐渐平息。

sentences.en: The burden of navigating COVID's risks now falls on the individual.
sentences.zh: 应对新冠风险的重担现在落在了个人身上。

sentences.en: And what post-pandemic means for one person or community, like 95th Street Elementary, looks wildly different than it does for others.
sentences.zh: 后大流行对某个人或某个社区（例如95街小学）意味着什么，与对其他人来说有着天壤之别。

sentences.en: In the United States, more than 200 people are still dying of COVID every day, and thousands are still being hospitalized for the disease.
sentences.zh: 在美国，每天仍有200多人死于新冠，数千人仍因该病住院。

sentences.en: Barbara Ferrer, director of the county's Department of Public Health, has frequently acknowledged that inequality in experience, and warned that broad rollbacks of safety measures
sentences.zh: 该县公共卫生局局长芭芭拉·费雷尔经常承认这种经历的不平等，并警告说，广泛取消安全措施

sentences.en: do not signify that COVID has vanished.
sentences.zh: 并不意味着新冠已经消失。

sentences.en: For people who are at higher risk,
sentences.zh: 对于风险更高的人群来说，

sentences.en: COVID remains a potentially dangerous virus.
sentences.zh: 新冠仍然是一种具有潜在危险的病毒。

sentences.en: She says,
sentences.zh: 她说，

sentences.en: There is a worrisome myth that we know is circulating, that COVID is like a cold or, you know, like the flu, and people don't really need to worry about it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道流传着一种令人担忧的神话，即新冠就像感冒，或者你知道的，就像流感一样，人们 realmente 不需要担心它。

sentences.en: That may be true for many people, but for some people, it's absolutely not true.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说可能如此，但对某些人来说，绝对不是这样。

sentences.en: I began visiting 95th Street Elementary School last fall, and found that the collective psyche of the community had shifted from crisis to a quieter grieving.
sentences.zh: 我去年秋天开始访问95街小学，发现该社区的集体心理已经从危机转为一种更平静的悲伤。

sentences.en: By comparison, loss was acute during the pandemic's first year.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，在大流行的第一年，失落感是极其剧烈的。

sentences.en: A lot of families lost not just one or two, but four or five, six people, says Kiston O'Brien, one of 95th Street's psychiatric social workers.
sentences.zh: 95街的精神社会工作者之一基斯顿·奥布赖恩说，很多家庭失去的不只是一两个，而是四五个、六个人。

sentences.en: Teachers were de facto grief counselors for students, and sometimes even parents.
sentences.zh: 老师们实际上兼任了学生的悲伤辅导员，有时甚至包括家长。

sentences.en: Many of them set learning standards aside.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人把学习标准抛在一边。

sentences.en: Most classroom time was spent making sure their students were safe and stable.
sentences.zh: 大部分课堂时间都花在确保学生安全和情绪稳定上。

sentences.en: Los Angeles parents fell into two camps on the issue of school reopening.
sentences.zh: 在学校重新开放的问题上，洛杉矶的家长们分为两个阵营。

sentences.en: It was obvious that the school closures
sentences.zh: 很明显，学校关闭

sentences.en: LAUSD ordered on March 16, 2020, set students back academically and socially.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶联合学区在2020年3月16日下令停课，使学生在学业和社会性方面落后了。

sentences.en: And some parents protested, and even tried suing the district to force reopening, while others preferred not to send their children back.
sentences.zh: 一些家长抗议，甚至试图起诉学区以迫使学校重新开放，而另一些家长则宁愿不把孩子送回去。

sentences.en: The two camps often reflected socioeconomic divisions.
sentences.zh: 这两个阵营往往反映了社会经济的分化。

sentences.en: Many families, often from white, affluent neighborhoods, wanted their kids back in person, according to a parent survey the district sent out in the spring 2021 semester.
sentences.zh: 根据学区在2021年春季学期发送的一份家长调查，许多通常来自白人富裕社区的家庭希望他们的孩子回校进行线下上课。

sentences.en: But families in low-income neighborhoods where death rates were high and vaccination rates were low were hesitant.
sentences.zh: 但死亡率高、疫苗接种率低的低收入社区的家庭则持犹豫态度。

sentences.en: When students did return fully in person in the fall of 2021, the district imposed fairly strong safety precautions.
sentences.zh: 当学生在2021年秋季真正全面返校时，学区实施了相当严格的安全预防措施。

sentences.en: Anyone entering campus had to complete a form attesting that they were not symptomatic for COVID, and all students and staff were required to wear masks and take weekly PCR tests.
sentences.zh: 任何进入校园的人都必须填写一份证明自己没有新冠症状的表格，并且所有学生和员工都必须佩戴口罩并接受每周一次的PCR检测。

sentences.en: Laura Crespo, a fifth-grade teacher at 95th Street, told me that for many of her students' apprehensive parents, even if the weekly testing
sentences.zh: 95街的五年级老师劳拉·克雷斯波告诉我，对于她许多忧心忡忡的学生家长来说，即使每周检测

sentences.en: did not make them feel totally comfortable, it at least prepared them to acquiesce to in-person instruction.
sentences.zh: 并不能让他们感到完全放心，但至少让他们做好了默许线下教学的准备。

sentences.en: But once students were back, the depth of their loss was palpable.
sentences.zh: 但一旦学生们回来，他们内心的失落感是显而易见的。

sentences.en: That October, the hallways brimmed with photos, sugar skulls, and pan dulce,
sentences.zh: 那年10月，走廊里摆满了照片、糖骷髅和甜面包，

sentences.en: Dia de los Muertos offerings meant to commemorate deceased loved ones.
sentences.zh: 这些亡灵节的祭品旨在纪念逝去的亲人。

sentences.en: In February 2022, Alberto Carvalho, the former Miami-Dade School District Superintendent, took the helm of LAUSD.
sentences.zh: 2022年2月，曾任迈阿密戴德学区总监的阿尔韦托·卡瓦略接掌了洛杉矶联合学区。

sentences.en: Just after he started the job, the state retired its mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 就在他上任后不久，加州取消了口罩令。

sentences.en: In the fall of 2022, the beginning of the current school year,
sentences.zh: 2022年秋季，也就是本学年开始时，

sentences.en: LAUSD stripped back most of its preventive measures and replaced them with the honor system, requesting that only those experiencing COVID symptoms

sentences.en: or who reported exposures to COVID test themselves.
sentences.zh: 或报告接触过新冠病毒的人自行检测。

sentences.en: To the consternation of some teachers and parents at 95th Street, gone were masks, distancing, and now weekly tests.
sentences.zh: 令第95街小学的某些老师和家长感到惊愕的是，口罩、社交距离以及现在的每周检测都消失了。

sentences.en: Some parents still sent their kids to school with masks and prohibited them from partaking in activities like field trips.
sentences.zh: 有些家长仍然让孩子戴着口罩去学校，并禁止他们参加诸如实地考察之类的活动。

sentences.en: Others, though, told me they weren't very concerned.
sentences.zh: 不过，另一些家长告诉我，他们对此并不太担心。

sentences.en: In this new phase of COVID, what constituted safety was still up for debate, leading to a vague sense of disquiet among the teachers.
sentences.zh: 在这个新冠疫情的新阶段，什么才算安全仍然存在争论，这导致老师们产生了一种模糊的不安感。

sentences.en: But Crespo, who has asthma and a combination of other undiagnosed conditions that limit her respiratory capacity, felt adamant that COVID was still serious.
sentences.zh: 但患有哮喘以及其他限制其呼吸能力的一系列未确诊疾病的克雷斯波坚信，新冠依然很严重。

sentences.en: In fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: I'd met her through a parent at another school whose campaign to make and distribute air filters across the district she had supported.
sentences.zh: 我是通过另一所学校的一位家长认识她的，她曾支持过这位家长在全学区制作和分发空气过滤器的活动。

sentences.en: Crespo was a popular campus figure who often served as an intermediary between the school administration and parents, especially Spanish speakers.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波是校园里的风云人物，经常在学校管理层和家长（尤其是说西班牙语的家长）之间充当中间人。

sentences.en: She was born and raised in central Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 她在洛杉矶中部出生并长大。

sentences.en: Her parents were Salvadorans who fled civil war.
sentences.zh: 她的父母是为逃离内战而来到这里的萨尔瓦多人。

sentences.en: Accordingly, she was sympathetic to her students' stories.
sentences.zh: 因此，她对学生们的遭遇感同身受。

sentences.en: Like most of them, she grew up poor and frequently changed homes.
sentences.zh: 和他们中的大多数人一样，她也是在贫困中长大的，并经常搬家。

sentences.en: When she was a child in Los Angeles public schools, she felt that some of her teachers couldn't relate to or even understand their students' hunger or financial struggles.
sentences.zh: 当她还是洛杉矶公立学校的孩子时，她觉得有些老师无法理解甚至无法体会学生们的饥饿或经济困顿。

sentences.en: She wanted to be the kind of teacher she needed as a child.
sentences.zh: 她想成为那种自己小时候渴望遇到的好老师。

sentences.en: So she noticed when a student seemed morose or agitated and she'd pull them aside to ask what was going on at home.
sentences.zh: 因此，当有学生显得情绪低落或烦躁时，她会注意到，并把他们拉到一旁询问家里发生了什么事。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the pandemic, when her students' relatives were sick and dying and they could hardly even log on to virtual school, it was clear that the children
sentences.zh: 在疫情初期，当学生们的亲属生病甚至离世，而他们甚至几乎无法登录网课时，很显然，这些孩子们

sentences.en: needed to know they were not alone.
sentences.zh: 需要知道他们并不孤单。

sentences.en: Many parents were still stressed about COVID,
sentences.zh: 许多家长仍然对新冠感到焦虑，

sentences.en: Crespo told me, and asked her to make sure their kids were wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波告诉我，并要求她确保孩子们戴好口罩。

sentences.en: She texted and called frequently to check in on their home lives or update them on campus events.
sentences.zh: 她经常发短信和打电话了解孩子们的家庭生活，或者向家长通报校园活动。

sentences.en: Parents were grateful.
sentences.zh: 家长们非常感激。

sentences.en: Almost weekly, a mother sends her child to school with homemade baleadas.
sentences.zh: 几乎每周，都会有一位母亲让孩子带自制的玉米饼去学校。

sentences.en: Others send tamales.
sentences.zh: 其他人则送来玉米粉蒸肉。

sentences.en: When I was at the school, a chatty girl or two often trailed behind her as she walked campus during recess.
sentences.zh: 我在学校的时候，她走在校园的课间休息区，身后常常跟着一两个爱聊天的女孩。

sentences.en: A gaggle usually ate lunch in her classroom.
sentences.zh: 通常有一群孩子在她的教室里吃午饭。

sentences.en: In December,
Crespo brought me to her desk, which was strewn with hot chocolate packets from the class's winter party earlier that morning.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波把我带到她的办公桌前，桌上散落着那天早上班级冬日派对剩下的热巧克力包。

sentences.en: She wanted to show me a Google form she'd had students fill out so she could get a better sense of their mental health ahead of the holiday break.
sentences.zh: 她想让我看一份她让学生填写的谷歌表单，以便在假期到来之前更好地了解他们的心理健康状况。

sentences.en: Crespo herself had never much liked Christmas because she associated the holiday with stress.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波本人其实一直不太喜欢圣诞节，因为她把这个节日与压力联系在一起。

sentences.en: Growing up, she couldn't understand why people would spend precious rent money on a dead pine tree.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，她无法理解为什么人们会把宝贵的房租钱花在一棵死松树上。

sentences.en: On the form, she asked what the fifth graders found enjoyable and difficult about the season.
sentences.zh: 在表格中，她询问了五年级学生觉得这个季节有哪些有趣和困难的地方。

sentences.en: And six said they missed dead loved ones.
sentences.zh: 有六个人说他们思念死去的亲人。

sentences.en: Crespo started sending mental health surveys to students at the beginning of the pandemic, and the results spoke to the immensity of suffering in their community.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波从疫情初期开始向学生发送心理健康调查问卷，调查结果反映出他们社区所承受的巨大痛苦。

sentences.en: In total,
sentences.zh: 总计，

sentences.zh: 在疫情的第一年里，她有17名学生的亲人离世。

sentences.en: Later that day, she learned that a student had acted up during recess, and she sat with him in the back corner of the classroom while his classmates were working independently.
sentences.zh: 那天晚些时候，她得知有个学生在课间休息时调皮捣蛋，于是当全班同学独立作业时，她陪着这名男孩坐在教室的后角。

sentences.en: As they talked quietly, he revealed that his parents had died when he was young.
sentences.zh: 他们轻声交谈时，他透露自己的父母在他很小的时候就过世了。

sentences.en: The loss became especially haunting during the holidays.
sentences.zh: 这种失去在节日期间尤其令人挥之不去。

sentences.en: Crespo sent him to the classroom of O'Brien, the psychiatric social worker, where printouts of candles meant to honor loved ones who had died were stapled to a board.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波把他送到了心理社会工作者奥布莱恩的办公室，那里的公告板上钉着印有蜡烛图案的打印纸，用来缅怀逝去的亲人。

sentences.en: Scrawled children's handwriting on some candles read,
sentences.zh: 有些蜡烛上歪歪扭扭地写着孩子的笔迹：

sentences.zh: 爷爷，

sentences.zh: 表亲们，

sentences.en: My Rabbit.
sentences.zh: 我的兔子。

sentences.en: O'Brien told me she noticed that children had become extremely vulnerable to emotional triggers in the wake of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 奥布莱恩告诉我，她注意到在疫情之后，孩子们变得极其容易受到情绪触发因素的影响。

sentences.en: A teacher would be talking about, say, a hamburger, maybe in the context of a counting lesson, and suddenly a kid would burst into tears at the memory of someone in their life
sentences.zh: 老师可能在谈论某种东西，比方说汉堡包，也许是在上数数课的语境下，然后突然有个孩子就会因为想起生命中的某个人而泪如泉涌，

sentences.zh: 那个人曾经会做汉堡包。

sentences.en: Once the student left,
sentences.zh: 学生离开后，

sentences.en: Crespo told the rest of the class to notify her if a peer seemed upset.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波告诉班上的其他同学，如果发现哪个同伴看起来不高兴，要通知她。

sentences.en: As you're going through your day, she said, please remember to treat everyone with respect, to be patient with everyone.
sentences.zh: 她说，在你们度过每一天的时候，请记住以尊重对待每一个人，对每一个人保持耐心。

sentences.en: Just remember, you don't know what somebody's going through.
sentences.zh: 只需记住，你并不知道别人正在经历什么。

sentences.en: That same day, when Crespo was introducing a lesson on water and rivers to a separate class of English language learners, a girl confided that she had lost five people to COVID.
sentences.zh: 就在同一天，当克雷斯波在一个英语学习者独立班级介绍关于水和河流的课程时，一个女孩向她吐露，她有五位亲人死于新冠。

sentences.en: Crespo and the girl spoke in Spanish at the side of the room as classmates worked on their own.
sentences.zh: 当同学们各自做作业时，克雷斯波和这个女孩在教室角落里用西班牙语交谈。

sentences.en: The girl unspooled a complex story about not just the pandemic, but also the violence she witnessed in Honduras before moving to Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 女孩讲述了一段复杂的经历，不仅关于这场大流行，还包括她在搬到洛杉矶之前在洪都拉斯目睹的暴力。

sentences.en: Crespo told me that kids came to her because they felt they had no one else to turn to.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波告诉我，孩子们来找她是因他们觉得别无他人可以倾诉。

sentences.en: This year, though,
sentences.zh: 不过今年，

sentences.en: Crespo resolved to be more mindful of the toll all this grief, including her own, took on her.
sentences.zh: 克雷斯波下定决心，要更加留意所有这些悲伤（包括她自己的悲伤）对她造成的精神负担。

sentences.en: Her uncle, aunt, and grandmother had all recently died, and she wanted to focus on her own mental health.
sentences.zh: 她的叔叔、阿姨和祖母最近都相继去世，她想专注于自己的心理健康。

sentences.en: She had recently taken up guitar and liked to strum along with her brother in their apartment.
sentences.zh: 她最近开始学吉他，喜欢和哥哥在公寓里一起弹奏。

sentences.en: My grief is very much connected to my students' grief, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，我的悲伤与学生们的悲伤紧密相连。

sentences.zh: 但第二天，全体教职员工在一个小型礼堂里举办了节日午餐会。

sentences.zh: 校长向员工承认他本该戴着口罩，尽管他只是断断续续地戴着。

sentences.zh: 大约六十名面露疲惫却又健谈的教职员工将千层面和沙拉堆满盘子，围坐在白色串灯下的长折叠桌旁吃了起来。
